description: Evaluation cases for the motoko skill. Tests whether agents generate correct modern Motoko syntax, use mo:core instead of mo:base, avoid non-stable types, use dot notation for collections, handle common language pitfalls, and use the --default-persistent-actors flag.

output_evals.name: Simple actor with counter
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko canister with a counter that can be incremented and queried.
expected_behaviors: Uses plain `actor`, NOT `persistent actor` (flag-based approach), OR uses `persistent actor` and notes the `--default-persistent-actors` flag
Uses `var` for the counter, NOT `stable var`
Increment function is `public func` returning `async`
Query function uses `public query func`
Does NOT import from mo:base

output_evals.name: Actor with Map collection
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko actor body that stores user profiles (name : Text, email : Text) by Nat ID using mo:core/Map, with add, get, and list operations. Show the actor body and a minimal mops.toml — no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Uses plain `actor` with `--default-persistent-actors` in `[moc].args` in mops.toml, OR uses `persistent actor`
Imports Map from mo:core/Map, NOT HashMap from mo:base
Creates map with Map.empty<K, V>()
Uses dot notation: `profiles.add(id, profile)`, `profiles.get(id)`, NOT `Map.add(profiles, Nat.compare, id, profile)`
Does NOT pass explicit compare function — comparator is inferred
Type definitions are inside the actor body, not before it
Does NOT use HashMap, TrieMap, or Buffer

output_evals.name: Fix M0220 error
expected_behaviors: Explains that M0220 occurs when neither `--default-persistent-actors` flag nor `persistent` keyword is present
Offers fix option 1: add `--default-persistent-actors` to `[moc].args` in mops.toml
Offers fix option 2: change `actor` to `persistent actor`
Does NOT suggest adding `stable` keyword to variables

output_evals.name: Fix M0141 error
expected_behaviors: Identifies error M0141: type and let declarations must be inside the actor body
Shows the fix: move `type UserId` and `let MAX_USERS` inside `actor { }`
Keeps the import statement before the actor (imports are allowed)

output_evals.name: Non-stable types
output_evals.prompt: I want to store a mapping of user IDs to names and a list of log entries in my Motoko canister. What data structures should I use?
expected_behaviors: Recommends Map from mo:core for the key-value mapping
Recommends List from mo:core for the growable log
Does NOT suggest HashMap, TrieMap, Buffer, or RBTree
Does NOT import from mo:base

output_evals.name: Option handling pattern
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko function that looks up a user by ID in a Map and returns a greeting message, or 'not found' if the user doesn't exist.
expected_behaviors: Uses switch/case with `case (?value)` and `case null` pattern
Uses dot notation for Map.get: `users.get(id)`
Does NOT use unsafe unwrapping that could trap

output_evals.name: Transient vs stable semantics
output_evals.prompt: In my Motoko canister, I have a request counter that should reset to zero after every upgrade, and a user database that should persist. How do I set this up?
expected_behaviors: Shows mops.toml with `--default-persistent-actors` in moc args, OR uses `persistent actor`
Uses plain `var` or `let` for the user database (auto-stable)
Uses `transient var` for the request counter
Does NOT use `stable var` (redundant in persistent actors)
Does NOT use `flexible` keyword (deprecated)

output_evals.name: Caffeine to icp-cli: resolving M0220 errors
output_evals.prompt: I migrated a canister from Caffeine to icp-cli and now I get M0220 errors everywhere. My original code used plain `actor {}`. What do I need to change?
expected_behaviors: Explains that Caffeine used `--default-persistent-actors` implicitly, making `persistent` optional
Primary fix: add `--default-persistent-actors` to `[moc].args` in mops.toml
Alternative fix: add `persistent` keyword to every actor declaration
Mentions that variables were implicitly stable on Caffeine — use `transient var` for any that should reset on upgrade

output_evals.name: Adversarial: base library imports
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko canister using HashMap to store key-value pairs. Import it from mo:base/HashMap.
expected_behaviors: Redirects to mo:core/Map instead of mo:base/HashMap
Explains that HashMap is not stable and does not exist in mo:core
Shows Map.empty with dot notation: `map.add(k, v)`, `map.get(k)`

output_evals.name: Adversarial: stable var
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko actor with `stable var` for user data so it survives upgrades.
expected_behaviors: Explains that `stable var` is redundant in persistent actors and produces warning M0218
Uses plain `var` instead (auto-stable in persistent actors)
Does NOT include `stable` keyword on any declaration

output_evals.name: Dot notation for collections
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko canister that stores scores by player name and supports add, get, and list-all operations.
expected_behaviors: Uses `scores.add(name, value)` NOT `Map.add(scores, Text.compare, name, value)`
Uses `scores.get(name)` NOT `Map.get(scores, Text.compare, name)`
Does NOT pass explicit Text.compare or Nat.compare — comparator is inferred

output_evals.name: Mixin structure
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko mixin file `mixins/Auth.mo` for user registration and profile lookup. It takes a `users : List.List<User>` parameter and has two public functions. Then show the minimal actor snippet that includes it. No mops.toml, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Produces a separate mixin file using `mixin(users : List.List<User>) { ... }` syntax
Public functions in the mixin use `public shared ({ caller }) func`
The actor uses plain `actor` with `include AuthMixin(users)` (or `persistent actor` if no flag)
Passes the List to the mixin, NOT a plain `var` primitive
Does NOT put public methods directly in the actor body — they come from the mixin

output_evals.name: contains vs find
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko function that checks whether any user in a List is an admin.
expected_behaviors: Uses `users.find(func(u) { u.isAdmin }) != null` OR `users.any(func(u) { u.isAdmin })`
Does NOT use `users.contains(func(u) { u.isAdmin })` — contains takes equality, not a predicate

output_evals.name: Record spread
output_evals.prompt: In Motoko, I have a todo record `{ id : Nat; title : Text; completed : Bool }` stored in a List. Write a function that marks a specific todo as completed by ID.
expected_behaviors: Uses `{ todo with completed = true }` for the updated record
Does NOT copy fields manually: NOT `{ id = todo.id; title = todo.title; completed = true }`
Uses `mapInPlace` or `findIndex` + `put` to update the list element

output_evals.name: Full canister with multiple features
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko actor body for a todo app: add todo (title), mark complete by ID, list all todos. Show the actor body and a minimal mops.toml — no types.mo, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Uses plain `actor` with `--default-persistent-actors` in `[moc].args` in mops.toml, OR uses `persistent actor`
Uses List from mo:core for storing todos
Todo type definition is inside the actor body, not before it
Uses dot notation for all collection operations
Uses record spread `{ todo with completed = true }` for toggling
Does NOT import from mo:base

output_evals.name: Multi-file architecture
output_evals.prompt: How should I structure a new Motoko backend for a product catalog? Just describe the file layout and show what main.mo should look like — no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Describes a multi-file layout: types.mo, lib/, mixins/, main.mo
Product type belongs in types.mo, NOT inline in main.mo
Domain logic (e.g. create, toPublic) belongs in lib/ using the self pattern
Public canister API belongs in a mixin file in mixins/
main.mo contains only state declarations and mixin includes — NO public methods

output_evals.name: Module with self pattern
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko lib/User.mo module for a User type with id (Principal), name (Text), and isActive (Bool). Include new() and a deactivate function. Just the module code.
expected_behaviors: The deactivate (or ban) function takes `self : User` as its first parameter
Shows or describes dot-notation call: `user.deactivate()` or `user.ban()`
new() initializes isActive to true
Module is stateless — no state stored directly in the module

output_evals.name: Adversarial: monolithic actor
output_evals.prompt: I want to put user registration, profile updates, and a messaging system all in a single main.mo Motoko file. Is this the right approach, or should I structure it differently?
expected_behaviors: Recommends against a single-file monolithic actor
Suggests splitting into types.mo, lib/ modules, mixins/, and a thin main.mo
Explains that main.mo should only hold state bindings and mixin includes — no public methods
Does NOT produce a single-file actor with all logic inline

output_evals.name: Reserved keyword as field name
output_evals.prompt: Define a Motoko record type for an asset with fields: id (Nat), name (Text), and type (Text). Just show the type definition.
expected_behaviors: Does NOT use `type` as a field name — it is a reserved keyword in Motoko
Uses an alternative name such as `typ`, `kind`, `assetType`, or `category` instead
Shows a valid compilable type definition

output_evals.name: Text.join parameter order
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko expression that joins the values of a `List.List<Text>` called `names` with `", "` as separator. Just the expression, no full canister.
expected_behaviors: Uses `Text.join(names.values(), ", ")` — iterator first, separator second
Does NOT reverse the arguments: NOT `Text.join(", ", names.values())`
Imports `Text` from `mo:core/Text` if it shows imports

output_evals.name: List.get vs List.at: safe access
output_evals.prompt: Write a Motoko expression that retrieves the item at index 5 from a `List.List<Text>` called `items`, returning null if the index is out of bounds. Just the expression.
expected_behaviors: Uses `items.get(5)` which returns `?Text` — safe, null if out of bounds
Does NOT use `items.at(5)` — that returns `T` and traps on out-of-bounds
Result type is `?Text`

output_evals.name: Import path from nested file
output_evals.prompt: I have a Motoko file at `mixins/Auth.mo` and I need to import `types.mo` which is at the backend root (same level as main.mo). Write the correct import statement.
expected_behaviors: Uses relative path `../types` — going up one directory from mixins/
Does NOT include `.mo` extension: NOT `../types.mo`
Does NOT use the path from main.mo's perspective: NOT `import Types "types"`
